narrative.northStar: The Ranch You're Walking Home Across
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Ranch You're Walking Home Across"**

The dashboard is a place, not a card grid. A layered flat-vector scene (sky, hazed hills, barn, silo, fence, trees, flowers, a dirt trail with a signpost per debt) fills the top of the main area, and the walk home along that trail is the real progress: the theme's friend sets off from the far hills and reaches the barn, with the "Debt-free" sign over its open door, on the day the last debt is paid. Debtsy and the other friends wait at the barn. Each of the nine themes is a time of day or a season on the same ranch. Everything below the scene sits on the scene's own ground color, so the page reads as the meadow in front of the picture.

Surfaces are soft, large-radius pages lifted by one diffuse tinted shadow. Headings are wooden plank tabs. Ink is a deep tint of the theme hue, never neutral black or gray. Type pairs a fat display face for the headline moment with a rounded friendly UI face; figures are tabular so money never jitters. The mood is warm, confident and playful without being babyish or bank-like. The animals (Debtsy and one friend per theme) stay as characters in the scene and in empty states.

Interior pages other than the dashboard get a short strip (132px phone, 150px tablet, 172px desktop) that carries a cropped piece of the same scene, a plank title and one action, then ordinary ranch cards below it.

### Home page: The Farm Stand

**Creative North Star: "The Stand Whose Chalkboard Does the Math"**

The home page is a roadside flower-and-berry stand, seen front-on. A scalloped striped awning runs across the top with the wordmark and two hanging tags on its valance, and a line of paper bunting hangs under it. Beneath sit two framed objects: a pale painted sign that carries the headline and the save tag, and a chalkboard in a wood frame that is the free calculator. The visitor's debts are the rows chalked on the board; the answer is a painted "Debt-free by" sign standing on the counter, whose letters roll over when a number changes. Debtsy works the register in every theme and nine friends work the counter or peek over the frames.

The page keeps going down the same stand: a paint rack on the counter front repaints everything in any of the nine app themes, three garden objects in the meadow carry the promises, a gingham cloth holds the two strategy seed packets, the questions are recipe cards taped up with washi tape, the Pro prices are a second chalkboard written as a menu, and a second painted sign closes the page. Every surface is a named physical material (paper, paint, chalk, wood, cloth, grass), and the mood is girly, abundant and warm without pressure: no timers, no urgency badges, no invented claims.
keyCharacteristics: The scene is the hero; modules follow on `--ranch-ground`.
One surface recipe: page-colored card, 24px radius, one soft tinted shadow, no borders.
Plank-tab headings with two nail dots on every module.
Ink and button colors are deep tints of the active theme; dark mode is derived, not separate.
Money is Quicksand 700 tabular; figures roll when they change.
Everything reads CSS custom properties, so a theme change or dark toggle needs no per-theme rules.
The calculator is the hero object and it works on arrival, with sample rows, real payoff math and no signup.
One stylesheet, nine paint jobs: every painted material reads a `--fs-*` property set on the page root.
Pressables are price tags, inputs are dashed chalk lines, dividers are bunting or a change of ground.
Sign faces stay pale with candy-colored lettering; the deep berry is an ink, never a sign background.
The page moves once on load, then only in answer to the visitor, plus a slow twinkle on the gold sparkles.
Rose Milk is the paint the page loads in; the pick is remembered on the device.

rules.name: The Tinted Ink Rule
rules.body: Text is never gray or black. It is the theme's deep ink or soft ink, so every theme and its night version keeps its hue.

rules.name: The One Alarm Rule
rules.body: Berry Focus is the single urgent color. It marks the focus debt, the next milestone and errors, and nothing decorative.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Components read `--ranch-*` only. A hex value in component CSS is a defect unless it is scene art.

rules.name: The Four Jobs Rule
rules.body: Bagel Fat One is for the headline moment and wordmark only. Fredoka names things, Nunito explains, Quicksand counts.

rules.name: The Rolling Figure Rule
rules.body: Money in the sky and today cards uses the RollingNumber digit-wheel; under reduced motion it shows the end state.

rules.name: The Soft Lift Rule
rules.body: One shadow recipe per surface class, always tinted by `--ranch-sh`. Never a black drop shadow, never a hard offset.

rules.name: The Paint Job Rule
rules.body: The stand's stylesheet holds no theme color. Every painted material reads a `--fs-*` property from the active palette, so a new surface is repainted by all nine themes without a per-theme rule. Fixed hex belongs only to art with a natural color.

rules.name: The Pale Sign Rule
rules.body: Sign faces are pale paper with Candy Ink lettering in every theme. Berry Ink is for text, outlines and small painted props; it is never the background of a sign.

rules.name: The Ink Follows the Surface Rule
rules.body: Text and focus rings take the ink of the material they sit on: Berry on paper, Chalk on boards, Counter Ink on the counter, the cloth inks on the gingham, Foot Ink on the grass. `scripts/stand-contrast.ts` checks each pairing against WCAG AA for all nine palettes (288 checks, none below AA at this build), and its alpha steps mirror the stylesheet's.

rules.name: The Chalk Hand Rule
rules.body: Anything written on a chalkboard is Quicksand with tabular figures or Bagel lettering, in Chalk or Chalk Gold. Nunito does not appear on a board.

rules.name: The Fits Its Sign Rule
rules.body: The painted date scales to its own length instead of wrapping or widening the sign.

rules.name: The Grounded Object Rule
rules.body: One contact shadow per object, tinted by `--fs-shade` (or `--fs-wood-shade` under wood). Nothing floats on a neutral black drop shadow.

rules.name: The Stand Object Rule
rules.body: A new element on the home page is a thing you would find at the stand (a tag, a sign, a board, a packet, a card, a marker). There are no generic cards, pills or badges here.

rules.name: The Register Rule
rules.body: Debtsy works the register in every theme; the theme's own friend gets the featured spot by the date sign.

rules.name: The One Arrival Rule
rules.body: The stand assembles once on load, then moves only in answer to the visitor. The twinkle is the only loop.

rules.name: The Calm Price Rule
rules.body: Money on the home page is stated as facts in chalk. No urgency badge, countdown or timer; a limited offer is a plain sentence.

dos: **Do** read surface, ink and state colors from `--ranch-*` tokens so all nine themes and dark mode work.
**Do** open every module and dialog with a plank heading.
**Do** keep money in Quicksand 700 tabular and wrap it in `.num`.
**Do** put the hero action ("Log a payment") in the sky and make it a pill in the button color.
**Do** use Berry Focus only for the thing to act on now.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px or more and give every animation a reduced-motion end state.
**Do** add new Tailwind-era markup to the shell's utility mapping only as a bridge; give the page proper ranch classes when you touch it.
**Do** paint every home page surface from `--fs-*` properties and add any new color role to all nine palettes in `palettes.ts`, then to the contrast script.
**Do** make pressables price tags, with Gold Leaf reserved for saving the plan or starting a free account.
**Do** write on boards in the chalk hand with tabular figures, and mark the chosen or computed thing in Chalk Gold.
**Do** keep the calculator usable on arrival with sample rows and real payoff math, and say "Never pays off" when that is the truth.
**Do** let the painted date re-letter only after typing settles, changing only the letters that differ.
**Do** declare motion under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` so the still page is complete.
**Do** keep Debtsy at the register and give the active theme's friend the featured spot.
donts: **Don't** lead a page with a big balance number over a grid of identical cards; the scene and trail come first.
**Don't** use gray text, black text or pure neutral backgrounds inside the shell.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows, card borders or nested cards.
**Don't** make it babyish, bank-like or plain; no gradient-pink pastel wash, no corporate blue dashboard.
**Don't** set Bagel Fat One below headline scale or in running UI text.
**Don't** reuse Berry Focus or the plank brown for decoration.
**Don't** copy the home page's Farm Stand materials (tags, chalkboards, awning, bunting) into the app interior.
**Don't** put a deep berry or burgundy background behind a sign; sign faces stay pale in every theme.
**Don't** write a theme color into the stand's stylesheet or hue-filter the postcard art.
**Don't** add urgency to prices: no "Limited!" badge, countdown or timer on the public page.
**Don't** bring Ranch cards, plank headings or pill buttons onto the home page, or stand materials into the app.
**Don't** rebuild the hero as a headline, a calculator card and a trust row; the board, the sign and the counter are the hero.
**Don't** set Nunito on a chalkboard or box a board input; fields are dashed chalk lines.
**Don't** add a second looping animation beside the twinkle.
